text.p: The Melbourne Institute's measure of Australian consumers inflationary expectations was unchanged at 4.1 percent in January from December.

"It appears that consumers are still hesitant about lowering their inflationary anticipations and the release of the next consumer price index figures on January 29 will confirm whether these fears are warranted or not," the institute said in a statement.
The January survey found that inflationary expectations varied according to occupation and age.

People employed in clerical, salesperson, personal service, plant and machine operator, driving and labouring occupations expected a higher inflation rate of 5.0 percent compared with people employed in managerial and administrative and professional jobs whose median expectation was 3.4 percent, the institute said.
Prime age (25 to 34 years) consumers had lower median expectations than older persons and young people, it said.
